scope: Bounded exact-owned local Docker lifecycle; injected process controls plus real pinned local containers.
logNormalization: Trailing blank lines removed; command output content preserved.
controls: Container create is separately acknowledged, exact immutable ID/name/image/owned/operation/run labels are inspected, and cancellation/deadline are checked before start/attach.

An unresolved create is never retried or started. Repeated missing inspections cannot establish cleanup without acknowledged or observed creation; unknown cleanup halts the batch and keeps its operation handle.
A controlled real Docker create completes only after the first cleanup inspection returns missing. Bounded cleanup discovers and removes the immutable ID, verifies absence, and no start is issued.

A real container with an expired guest deadline exits without invoking candidate source. The retained BusyBox timer test also limits a far-future wall deadline to a one-second cap and observes exit 137 before a longer host timeout.
Cancellation from the operation journal and an exhausted image-inspection allowance prevent creation. Removal failure preserves the observed immutable identity.
Existing parent-death launcher, exact-run restart recovery, no-overlap, host comparison and read-only/no-network containment controls pass.

bounds.creationTimeout: At most min(10 seconds, remaining monotonic batch wall). Image inspection, ownership inspection and start use the same remaining batch allowance.
bounds.cleanup: Separate 5-second monotonic deadline; each inspect/removal uses at most the remaining deadline and at most 1 second. Original aborted signal is not reused.
bounds.guest: Absolute wall deadline plus a finite positive duration cap no greater than the originally validated remaining allowance; original BusyBox SIGKILL timer remains.
bounds.cpu: Local quota remains 0.5 CPU; measured CPU remains unknown. These tests do not establish paid or evaluated CPU matching.

officialDocumentation.verifiedBy: parent coordinator; create does not start, prints ID and supports the retained flags
parent coordinator; attach and interactive flags

limitations: The origin of the previously observed Created container is unknown. The late-create test controls the completion order with an injected process wrapper and real Docker create/remove; it does not reproduce the original natural daemon race.

Finite cleanup polling cannot prove no accepted daemon create will appear later. An unobserved create remains unconfirmed; if it appears after cleanup or owner death it is inert because this runner never issued start.

reconcileContainers(runIds) remains unchanged. Run-ID listing and removal prove only the observed snapshot, not daemon request quiescence or atomic crash cleanup. Later exact-run reconciliation may still be required.
Parent-death protection stops the CLI; it does not cancel accepted daemon requests. Already-started containers rely on the guest bound and exact-owned recovery.
No provider, credential, existing evaluator workspace, sealed fixture, gold data or paid resource was accessed. Candidate Python ran only inside task-owned local containers.
All removal actions target exact test-owned names or independently verified immutable IDs; no project-wide destructive cleanup was performed.

notRun.reason: Parent performs one integrated run after source and independent-review integration.

notRun.check: Physical power-loss recovery or unbounded daemon delay
notRun.reason: Not proven by these finite local process and container controls.
Out of scope; no provider calls or evaluator corpus access authorized.
